name: cross_listed_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Stocks listed on both NSE and BSE can exhibit transient price divergences of 2-10 bps due to differential order flow, varying market microstructure (NSE has higher HFT participation), and latency differences between exchange matching engines. While professional arbitrageurs keep the spread tight on large-caps, mid-cap stocks (market cap ₹5000-20000 cr) with lower BSE volume have exploitable divergences that persist for 1-5 minutes. The edge exists because BSE has lower participation from algorithmic traders, creating stale quotes that diverge from NSE price discovery. The inefficiency persists because dual-exchange execution requires co-location on both exchanges, which is expensive for retail.
universe: Liquid mid-cap stocks listed on both NSE and BSE (e.g., VOLTAS, GODREJCP, MPHASIS)
stock_filter: market cap ₹5000-20000 cr; NSE volume > ₹50cr/day; BSE volume > ₹5cr/day; listed on both exchanges

conditions: price_diff_bps > 5 (NSE trading higher than BSE by >5bps)
long.confirmation: buy on BSE, sell on NSE simultaneously when diff exceeds 5bps

conditions: price_diff_bps < -5 (BSE trading higher than NSE by >5bps)
short.confirmation: buy on NSE, sell on BSE simultaneously when diff exceeds 5bps

entry.entry_price: limit orders at mid-price on both exchanges, aggressive side first

exit.stop_loss: price_diff_bps exceeds 15bps against position OR loss > 0.2%
exit.trailing_stop: none (trades are too short for trailing stops)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 10 mins (if arb hasn't closed, something structural)
exit.eod_rule: flatten all positions by 15:25 IST (ensure settlement on both exchanges)
exit.signal_exit: if combined_spread_bps widens > 15bps during trade, exit (liquidity drying up)

risk.position_sizing: equal INR notional on each exchange, same number of shares on each leg

filters.vix_filter: none (arb works in all VIX regimes)
filters.time_filter: best windows: 09:20-10:00 and 14:30-15:25 (open/close have more BSE dislocations)
filters.volume_filter: BSE 1-min volume must be > 500 shares (minimum for executable arb)
filters.spread_filter: combined bid-ask spread across both exchanges < 8bps
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has corporate action affecting settlement on either exchange
other_filters: skip if BSE has had exchange outage or slowdown alerts today

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — as BSE improves matching engine speed and more arb bots enter, divergences will shrink

weaknesses: BSE liquidity for mid-caps is extremely thin; large orders can move the BSE price against you, and fills may be partial or delayed
Zerodha doesn't support true simultaneous cross-exchange execution; the latency between placing NSE and BSE orders creates leg risk
Settlement and clearing across two exchanges adds operational complexity; T+1 settlement mismatches can occur
prior_art: Gagnon & Karolyi (2010) cross-listing price parity; adapted for NSE-BSE dual listing. Similar to Subrahmanyam (1994) on multi-market microstructure.
notes: Edge math: 0.75 * 5bps - 0.25 * 8bps = 3.75 - 2.0 = 1.75bps gross per trade. Costs per trade ~6bps RT (both exchanges). Net negative per trade! Edge relies on high frequency (10+ trades/day) and capturing the 5bps+ divergences that occur during volatile opens. The 20bps daily estimate assumes 10 trades with avg 2bps net. Realistically marginal. Needs very low latency to work.
